issues.failure_explanation: The backward identity satisfied by the implemented recursion is $Y^{\pi,\theta}_{t_{i-1}} + \int_{t_{i-1}}^{t_i}Z^{\pi,\theta}dB = \mathcal C^{\theta(i)}(F^{\pi,\theta}_i)$, which by Remark rmk:stepwise-kernels-smooth equals $Y^{\pi,\theta}_{t_i} + \Delta_i\mathcal C^{P}(f^{\pi,\theta}_i)$, not $Y^{\pi,\theta}_{t_i} + \Delta_i f^{\pi,\theta}_i$ as the proof states. The Malliavin derivative of the projection therefore brings the residual $\Delta_i D_s[f^{\pi,\theta}_i - \mathcal C^{P}(f^{\pi,\theta}_i)]$ into the differentiated equation, which the proof never accounts for; the chain-rule estimate \eqref{eq:Df-chain-rule-bound} is applied to a generator term that does not appear in the identity being differentiated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Differentiate the correct identity $Y^{\pi,\theta}_{t_{i-1}} + \int_{t_{i-1}}^{t_i}Z^{\pi,\theta}dB = \mathcal C^{P,M(i)}(F^{\pi,\theta}_i)$ and use the Malliavin commutation $D\mathcal C^{P}(f) = \mathcal C^{P-1}(Df)$ (Lemma \ref{proposition inequality chaos truncation} (ii)) together with the contraction property of the chaos projection to bound $E\|D\mathcal C^{P}(f^{\pi,\theta}_i)\|^2 \le E\|D f^{\pi,\theta}_i\|^2$; the same recursion then yields \eqref{eq:energy-estimates-Malliavin-Y-Z} and \eqref{eq:energy-estimates-malliavin-f} unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The energy estimates \eqref{eq:energy-estimates-Malliavin-Y-Z} and \eqref{eq:energy-estimates-malliavin-f}, and through them the $\mathbb E(\|D\xi\|^2)/(P+1)$ term of Theorem thm:added-4, are not established by the displayed proof; the lemma's conclusion is nevertheless recoverable, so no formal statement is definitively false, but the proof as written is invalid.
issues.title: Malliavin-energy lemma proved by differentiating an identity the implemented scheme does not satisfy
issues.why_classification: A short local substitution (differentiate the identity involving $\mathcal C^{P}(f^{\pi,\theta}_i)$ instead of $f^{\pi,\theta}_i$) together with the contraction $\|\mathcal C^{P-1}Df\|\le\|Df\|$ already proved in the paper repairs the proof; the lemma's statement, its constant, and all downstream uses remain intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Through this section we make use of the following notation and assumptions. Let $\pi \subset [0,T]$ be a partition such that $\max_{i} \Delta_i / \Delta_{i+1} \leq L$. Let $\theta = (P,M) \in \mathbb{N}^{2}$. Let Assumption \ref{assumption 1} be satisfied.

issues.failure_explanation: The preamble to Section 4.3 imposes only 'Assumption \ref{assumption 1}' (Lipschitz generator, $\xi \in L^2$) plus mesh regularity, and Theorems \ref{thm:added-4} and \ref{thm:added-5} assert bounds containing $C\abs{\pi}$ and $\mathbb E(\norm{D\xi}_{\mathbb H_T}^{2})/(P+1)$. However, the $O(\abs{\pi})$ term comes from Theorem \ref{Theorem main convergence rate}, which is proved only under Assumption \ref{main assumption convergence rate} ($\xi \in \mathbb D^{2,q}_T$ with Hölder regularity of $D\xi$, $f \in C^{1:2}_{b,(y,z)}$ and $f$ Hölder-$1/2$ in $t$), and the chaos-truncation terms require $\xi \in \mathbb D^{1,2}_T$ and $f \in C^{1:1}_{b,(y,z)}$ (Lemma \ref{lem:malliavin-energy}). Under Assumption \ref{assumption 1} alone the Malliavin derivative $D\xi$ need not exist and the rate $C\abs{\pi}$ is not available, so the theorems as stated are not established by the paper's results.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State Theorems \ref{thm:added-4} and \ref{thm:added-5} under the Malliavin-regularity hypotheses actually used in their derivation (Assumption \ref{main assumption convergence rate} for the $\abs{\pi}$-rate, $f \in C^{1:1}_{b,(y,z)}$ for the energy estimates, and $\xi \in \mathscr{A}^{P}_{T}$ for the $M$-truncation term), i.e. add the missing hypotheses to the theorem statements so that they match the arguments.
issues.overall_effect: Both main error estimates (Theorems thm:added-4 and thm:added-5) overstate their scope: for merely Lipschitz data with square-integrable terminal condition the asserted bound is neither meaningful ($\mathbb E\norm{D\xi}_{\mathbb H_T}^2$ may be undefined/infinite) nor derivable from the proofs, which silently use the regularity of Assumption \ref{main assumption convergence rate}.
issues.title: Main error theorems claim rates for data satisfying only Assumption 1, while their derivation requires Malliavin regularity
issues.why_classification: The repair is a hypothesis-level restriction: with the standard Malliavin regularity added, the same rates and the same algorithmic guarantees survive, so a recognizably comparable theorem remains; no new proof architecture is needed, but the advertised 'arbitrary square-integrable terminal condition' regime must be excluded from the quantitative statement.

issues.failure_explanation: The remark asserts that Assumption \ref{assumption 1} implies $\xi \in L^4$ and hence $\mathbf V_m(\xi) < \infty$. Assumption \ref{assumption 1}(iii) only requires $\xi \in L^{2}(\mathcal F_T)$, which does not imply $\mathbb E(|\xi|^4) < \infty$: for example $\xi = g(B_T)$ with $g(x)=|x|^{-\alpha}\mathbf 1_{\{\abs{x}\le 1\}}$ and $\tfrac14<\alpha<\tfrac12$ is square-integrable but has $\mathbb E\abs{\xi}^{4}=\infty$, and then $a!\,\overline{\mathbb V}(\xi\, H_a^{(m,0)})$ need not be finite, so $\mathbf V_m(\xi)=\infty$ is possible. Thus the finiteness claimed in the remark is not guaranteed by the stated hypotheses.

failure_location.quote: Under Assumption \ref{assumption 1}, the random variable $\xi$ has absolute moments of fourth order, and hence $\mathbf{V}_{m}(\xi)$ can be proven to be finite.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add an explicit integrability requirement (e.g. $\xi \in L^{4}(\mathcal F_T)$, or directly $\mathbf V_m(\xi)<\infty$) to the hypotheses of Theorem \ref{thm:added-5} and delete or weaken the prose claim in the remark.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that $\mathbf V_m(\xi)$ is finite under Assumption \ref{assumption 1} is false in general; consequently the right-hand side of the estimate in Theorem \ref{thm:added-5} need not be finite for admissible data, and the Monte-Carlo error bound loses its content unless extra integrability of $\xi$ is assumed.
issues.title: Fourth moments of the terminal condition claimed under a square-integrability assumption
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard local condition ($\xi \in L^4$) restores the claim and all guarantees of the theorems remain intact with the same rates; only an incorrect explanatory remark must be retracted.
